A cloud container is an isolated software environment on a remote server used to run an application or task.
Cloud credentials concept
Cloud credentials are passwords, keys, or tokens used to access cloud services and resources.
Cloud data concept
Data stored in online services run on remote servers rather than only on a local device.
Cloud Enumeration technique
Cloud enumeration is the process of identifying cloud accounts, services, resources, and settings that may be accessible.
cloud environment concept
A cloud environment is a set of computing resources, applications, and data hosted on internet-based infrastructure instead of only local machines.
Cloud Logging product
Cloud Logging is Google Cloud’s service for collecting, storing, and analyzing logs from cloud resources and applications.
Cloud Logs concept
Records generated by cloud services that show events such as sign-ins, configuration changes, and system activity.
cloud metadata concept
Cloud metadata is information about cloud resources, such as instance settings or credentials, that cloud services make available to systems.
Cloud Posture concept
Cloud posture is the overall security state of an organization's cloud services and settings.
cloud provider concept
A cloud provider is a company that offers computing services such as servers, storage, and databases over the internet.
cloud providers organization
Cloud providers are companies that rent computing services such as servers, storage, databases, and networking over the internet.
cloud resources concept
Cloud resources are computing services like servers, storage, databases, or apps that run in an internet-hosted cloud environment.
also: publicly available cloud resources
cloud services concept
Computing resources—like storage, apps, and networking—delivered over the internet by providers such as AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
Cloud-First IR Capability concept
A cloud-first incident-response capability is an organization's ability to investigate and handle security incidents in cloud systems.
also: IR solution
cloudflare
Cloudflare is a company that provides content delivery, DDoS protection, DNS, and web security services.
Cloudflare Tunnel product
Cloudflare Tunnel is a Cloudflare service that lets a server be reached through Cloudflare without opening inbound ports directly to the internet.
Cloudflare WARP product
Cloudflare's VPN-like service that routes a device's internet traffic through Cloudflare's network.
Cloudflare Workers product
Cloudflare Workers is a Cloudflare product that lets developers run small pieces of code on Cloudflare’s global network.
also: Cloudflare Workers host, p-luce2oan[.]workers[.]dev
cluster concept
A group of connected computers or appliances that work together as one system.
ClusterRole concept
A ClusterRole is a Kubernetes permission definition that can grant access across an entire cluster.
CMS product
A CMS, or content management system, is software used to create and manage website content.
also: Content Management System
code execution technique
Code execution means an attacker can make a computer or server run commands or software of their choosing.
coding concept
Coding is writing instructions in a programming language so a computer can perform tasks.
Coding Challenge concept
A coding challenge is a programming task used to test a developer's technical skills.
also: take-home coding exercise
coding tests concept
Coding tests are programming exercises that employers may use to evaluate job applicants.
Coding Tools product
Coding Tools is a StepSecurity product area for finding and managing software-development tools on organizational devices.
Collabora organization
A software company known for developing and supporting office-document collaboration software.
Collection product
A saved grouping feature that automatically gathers internet assets matching a defined search query.
com.jamf.alme other
com.jamf.alme is the bundle identifier used by macOS to uniquely identify Jamf's ALME application.
com.jamf.alme.agent.plist tool
com.jamf.alme.agent.plist is a macOS configuration file used to start the Jamf alme-agent process.
com.jamf.alme.plist tool
com.jamf.alme.plist is a macOS configuration file used to start the Jamf ALME background service.
Command Line concept
A text-based way to control a computer by typing commands instead of clicking buttons.
Community Edition product
Community Edition usually means a free or limited version of a software product offered for individual or community use.
Compact discs product
Round optical discs that can store digital files, music, or software.
Compensating Control concept
A compensating control is an alternative security safeguard used when the ideal fix cannot be applied right away.
also: compensating controls
compiler tool
A compiler is a program that turns human-written code into software a computer can run.
compromise concept
A compromise is a situation where a system, account, or data has been breached or taken over by an attacker.
compromised concept
Compromised means a system, account, or device has been accessed or controlled by someone who should not have access.
compromised credentials concept
Compromised credentials are login details that have been stolen, exposed, or otherwise made unsafe.
computer systems concept
Computer systems are connected hardware and software used to process information and provide digital services.
Concurrently concept
Concurrently means performing multiple tasks at the same time or in overlapping time periods.
conditional-access
Conditional access is a security policy that allows or blocks logins based on risk, device, location, or other conditions.
Confidence concept
Confidence is a measure of how certain a security team is that an alert or finding is truly malicious.
Configuration drift concept
Configuration drift happens when systems slowly change from their intended settings over time, creating security or reliability risks.
configuration files concept
Configuration files are files that store settings telling software or systems how to behave.
Configurations concept
Configurations are the settings that determine how software, systems, or security tools behave.
connected devices concept
Connected devices are everyday or business devices that can communicate over a network or the internet, such as phones, cameras, sensors, or appliances.
Connecting concept
Connecting is a status meaning a device, app, or service is trying to establish a network connection.
connectivity concept
The set of systems, data, permissions, and services that a user, application, or AI agent can reach.
Consent concept
A person's informed agreement to let an organization collect, use, or share their information.
conspiracy concept
Conspiracy is an agreement between people to commit an unlawful act.
Contact Details concept
Information used to contact a person, such as an address, email address, or phone number.
Contact information concept
Contact information means details like an email address, phone number, or mailing address that can be used to reach someone.
Contagious Interview technique
Contagious Interview is a North Korea-linked campaign that tricks job seekers or developers into running malicious software during fake interviews.
also: Contagious Interview (DPRK)
container concept
A container is a lightweight package that runs an application with its needed files in an isolated environment.
container image scanning technique
A security practice that examines container images for vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and malware before deployment.
containers concept
Containers are lightweight packages that run applications with their needed files in isolated environments.
containment technique
Containment is the process of limiting a cyber incident so attackers or malware cannot spread further.
context concept
Context is extra information about an access request, such as where it comes from or what conditions surround it.
continuous concept
In security, continuous means something is monitored or updated all the time instead of only during occasional checks.
Contractor concept
A person or company hired to perform work for an organization without being its regular employee.
Control coverage concept
Control coverage measures how much of an organization's environment is protected or monitored by specific security controls.
Controller concept
A controller is a component that manages or directs how other parts of a system behave.
coordination concept
Coordination is the organized sharing of tasks, information, and decisions among people or teams.
Core component concept
A core component is an essential part of a system that other functions depend on.
Corporate Applications concept
Software and online services used by employees to do work for their organization.
corporate network concept
A corporate network is the private collection of computers, servers, and systems used by an organization.
corporate networks concept
Corporate networks are the connected computers, servers, and systems used by a company.
counterterrorism concept
Counterterrorism means efforts to prevent, disrupt, or respond to terrorist activity.
credential concept
A credential is proof of identity for logging in, such as a password, security token, API key, or certificate.
credential rotation technique
Credential rotation means replacing passwords, keys, or tokens with new ones to reduce the risk from stolen or old credentials.
Credential Spraying technique
An attack that tries a few common passwords against many accounts to avoid triggering login protections.
credential theft technique
Credential theft is the stealing of usernames, passwords, tokens, or other login information.
credential-harvesting
Credential harvesting is collecting usernames, passwords, or login tokens from victims.
credentials concept
Credentials are login details or access tokens that prove a user or system is allowed to access something.
Credit model concept
A pricing system in which users spend credits to perform different actions in a service.
credit reports concept
Credit reports are records of your borrowing and repayment history used by lenders to judge financial risk.
critical systems concept
Critical systems are important systems whose failure could seriously affect operations or safety.
cron tool
cron is a Unix tool that runs scheduled commands or scripts automatically at set times.
cron jobs tool
Cron jobs are scheduled tasks on Unix-like systems that automatically run commands at set times.
crontab tool
crontab is a Unix/Linux file or command used to schedule tasks to run automatically at set times.
crowdstrike organization
CrowdStrike is a cybersecurity company known for endpoint protection, threat intelligence, and incident response.
crypto assets concept
Crypto assets are digital assets such as cryptocurrencies or tokens that use blockchain-related technology.
crypto wallet product
A crypto wallet is software or hardware that stores the keys needed to control cryptocurrency.
Crypto-Theft concept
Crypto-theft is the stealing of cryptocurrency, wallet keys, seed phrases, or access tokens from victims.
CryptoBilis organization
A reseller organization that sells cryptocurrency hardware products.
cryptocurrency concept
Cryptocurrency is digital money, such as Bitcoin, that uses cryptography and usually runs on a blockchain.
cryptocurrency accounts concept
Cryptocurrency accounts are wallets or exchange accounts used to hold, send, or receive digital assets.
Cryptocurrency exchange concept
An online service where people can buy, sell, trade, or store digital currencies.
cryptocurrency thefts concept
Cryptocurrency thefts are crimes where attackers steal digital currencies such as Bitcoin or Ethereum.
cryptocurrency wallet product
A cryptocurrency wallet is software or hardware used to store and use the keys that control digital coins.
cryptocurrency wallets product
Cryptocurrency wallets are tools used to store and manage access to digital currency funds.
Cumulative updates concept
Cumulative updates are software updates that include current fixes plus earlier fixes in one package.
cursor
Cursor is an AI-assisted code editor built for software developers.
also: SpaceXAI-owned company
Cursor IDE product
Cursor IDE is an AI-assisted code editor based on Visual Studio Code.
customer data concept
Customer data is information a company keeps about its customers, such as names, contact details, or purchase history.
customer information concept
Customer information is data a business keeps about its customers, such as names, contact details, purchases, or account records.
also: information, data
Customer Names concept
Names that identify customers and may be sensitive when exposed in a data breach.
Customer origin-facing proxies concept
Proxy systems that sit between customers' origin servers and the internet to handle incoming or outgoing web traffic.
also: outbound service
CVE vulnerability
A CVE is a public identifier used to track a specific known software vulnerability.
CVE identifier concept
A CVE identifier is the standard public tracking number assigned to a known cybersecurity vulnerability.
CVSS concept
CVSS is a standard scoring system used to rate how severe a software vulnerability is.
CVSS 10.0 concept
CVSS 10.0 is the highest severity score on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System scale for rating security flaws.
CVSS score concept
A CVSS score is a standard number used to show how severe a software vulnerability is.
also: CVSS score of 8.1, CVSS 8.6
Cyber campaigns technique
Coordinated sets of online attacks or influence activities carried out over time toward a shared goal.
Cyber disruptions concept
Cyber disruptions are interruptions to normal operations caused by digital failures, attacks, outages, or security incidents.
cyber incident concept
A cyber incident is any event where digital systems, accounts, or data may have been attacked, exposed, or disrupted.
also: attack
cyber incidents concept
Cyber incidents are events that threaten or harm computer systems, networks, or data.
Cyber's Most Wanted List concept
An FBI list that publicizes people wanted for alleged major cybercrime and may offer rewards for information about them.
also: Cyber's Most Wanted
cyberattack concept
A cyberattack is an attempt to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems or data.
cyberattacks concept
Malicious activities conducted over computer networks to steal data, disrupt operations, or damage systems.
cybercriminals threat-actor
Cybercriminals are people who use computers or the internet to commit crimes such as fraud, theft, or extortion.
also: hackers
Cybersecurity concept
Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computers, networks, software, and data from digital attacks or misuse.
cybersecurity incident concept
A cybersecurity incident is an event that threatens the security of systems, networks, or data.
also: cyber threats, cloud security breach, real incident, confirmed incidents
Data access concept
Data access means the ability to view, use, change, or retrieve information from a system.
data breach concept
A data breach is an incident where sensitive, private, or protected information is accessed, exposed, or stolen without permission.
data centers concept
Data centers are facilities full of servers and networking equipment that run websites, cloud services, and business systems.
Data collection concept
Data collection is the process of gathering information from people, systems, devices, or services for analysis or use.
Data destruction technique
The deliberate deletion, corruption, or wiping of data so it cannot be used.
Data Events concept
Data events are logged actions involving data, such as reading, changing, deleting, or exporting it.
data exfiltration technique
Data exfiltration is the unauthorized removal or copying of data from a system.
Data Retention Practices concept
Data retention practices are rules and procedures for deciding how long an organization keeps information and logs.
also: retention period, retention of data
Data Sources concept
Data sources are systems, services, or devices from which information is collected.
also: cloud data source, multiple sources
Data Structures concept
Data structures are ways of organizing information so computers and people can store and use it.
also: schemas, data formats, semantics
data theft concept
Data theft is the stealing of information from a system or service.
Data Transmission concept
Data transmission is the sending of information from one device or system to another.
Database-Level Logs concept
Database-level logs are records of actions occurring inside a database, such as queries, logins, and changes to data.
DataSuckers threat-actor
DataSuckers is a threat-actor group referenced in security reporting.
Dates of birth concept
Dates of birth are personal information that can help identify someone and may be sensitive if exposed.
Debian product
A well-known community-driven Linux distribution famous for its stability and package management system.
also: Debian 12 (Bookworm), Debian 13 (Trixie), Debian testing, Debian unstable
Debian 12 product
Debian 12 is a version of the Debian Linux operating system, also known by the codename Bookworm.
DebugBear organization
A website-performance monitoring service that helps organizations measure and improve website speed and user experience.
deception technique
Deception is tricking a person or system into believing something false, often to gain access or hide activity.
Declarative Device Management protocol
An Apple device-management approach in which devices automatically apply desired settings and report their status.
also: DDM
Deepfaked Panel technique
A deepfaked panel is a group of people shown in an audio or video interaction using AI-generated or manipulated media to appear real.
DeepSeek organization
DeepSeek is an AI service provider referenced in the article.
Defend concept
Defend means to protect systems, networks, data, or users from cyber threats.
defenders concept
Defenders are the people or teams responsible for protecting systems and responding to cyber threats.
Delegation concept
Delegation is the act of giving another account, service, or smart contract permission to perform actions on one's behalf.
deleted concept
Deleted means removed from normal access, though copies may sometimes still exist in backups, logs, or recovery areas.
Demographic information concept
Basic descriptive data about people, such as age, gender, location, or other population characteristics.
denial-of-service
Denial-of-service is an attack that overwhelms a system so legitimate users cannot access it.
denial-of-service (DoS) condition concept
A situation where a system becomes unavailable or unusable, often because it is overloaded or crashed.
also: DoS
denial-of-service condition concept
A denial-of-service condition is a situation where a system becomes unavailable or unusable for legitimate users.
Department of Justice organization
The main U.S. federal law enforcement agency responsible for prosecuting federal crimes and upholding justice.
Designated account concept
A specific account selected to receive funds, data, or other transfers.
desktop app product
A desktop app is software installed on a laptop or desktop computer.
Detect technique
Detect means to identify suspicious or malicious activity in systems, networks, or data.
Detect mode technique
A security-tool setting that records or alerts on suspicious activity without blocking it.
detection concept
Detection is the process of finding signs of suspicious or malicious activity.
detection rule concept
A detection rule is a set of instructions a security tool uses to spot suspicious activity or known threats.
also: detection rules, rule
Detection, Investigation and Response concept
Detection, investigation and response are the security activities of finding threats, determining what happened, and taking action to contain them.
detections concept
Alerts or findings generated by security tools indicating that a potential threat or malicious activity has been identified.
also: custom detections, predetermined detections
deterministic concept
A system or function that always produces the same output for the same input, with no random variation.
Dev Machine Guard tool
Dev Machine Guard is a security tool or product name referenced in reporting.
also: StepSecurity Dev Machine Guard, Community agent, open-source agent
Developer credentials concept
Developer credentials are usernames, passwords, keys, or tokens that let someone access software development systems such as code repositories or build servers.
Developer Device concept
A computer used by a software developer to write, test, or manage code.
Developer Endpoints concept
Developer endpoints are the laptops, desktops, or other devices used by people who create software.
Developer laptops concept
Developer laptops are computers used by software developers to write, test, and manage code, which can make them valuable targets for attackers.
Developer machines concept
Developer machines are computers used by software developers to write, build, and test code.
Developer Signature concept
A developer signature is a digital proof that software was signed by a particular software publisher and has not been altered.
also: signature
Device-code authentication protocol
Device-code authentication is a login method where one device shows a code that the user enters on another device to approve access.
device-code-phishing technique
Device-code phishing tricks users into entering a legitimate login code that gives attackers access to their account.
device_code protocol
device_code is a code used behind the scenes in OAuth device login to identify the device waiting for user approval.
Devices downloaded technique
Devices whose stored data has been copied for examination or investigation.
DevOps concept
DevOps is a way of working where software development and IT operations teams collaborate to build, deploy, and run software faster.
DevOps engineer's laptop concept
A laptop used by an engineer who helps build, deploy, and operate software systems.
DevOps Laptop product
A DevOps laptop is a computer used by an engineer who manages software deployment and computing infrastructure.
also: engineer’s machine, developer’s machine
Diameter protocol
Diameter is a telecom authentication and signaling protocol used in modern mobile networks such as 4G.
also: Diameter-based attacks, Diameter updates
DigiCert organization
DigiCert is a company that issues digital certificates used to secure websites, software, and online identities.
DigiNotar organization
A former Dutch certificate authority known for a major compromise in which fraudulent certificates were issued.
digital assets concept
Digital assets are valuable items that exist electronically, such as cryptocurrency, tokens, files, or online accounts.
digital certificates concept
Digital certificates are electronic credentials that help prove a website, device, or user is who they claim to be.
digital wallets product
Digital wallets are apps or services that store payment information, cryptocurrency keys, or other digital assets.
DirectAccess product
DirectAccess is a Microsoft remote-access technology that automatically connects managed devices to a corporate network.
also: legacy DirectAccess technology
Disclosure concept
Disclosure is the act of reporting or publishing information about a security issue so it can be understood and fixed.
Discovery technique
Discovery is the attacker activity of learning about a victim’s systems, accounts, and network before taking further action.
disruption concept
Disruption is an interruption that prevents systems, services, or operations from working normally.
distinct() technique
A data-processing operation that removes duplicate entries from a dataset.
DKIM protocol
DKIM is an email signing method that helps verify that a message was authorized by a domain and was not changed after signing.
DMARC protocol
DMARC is an email policy check that uses SPF or DKIM alignment to help determine whether a message claiming to come from a domain should be trusted.
DNS protocol
DNS is the internet system that turns human-readable names like example.com into the numeric addresses computers use to find websites and services.
Dodo Pizza organization
Dodo Pizza is a Russian pizza restaurant chain.
doj organization
DOJ usually refers to the U.S. Department of Justice, the federal agency responsible for law enforcement and legal affairs in the United States.
domain concept
A domain is a human-readable internet name, such as example.com, used to find websites and services.
also: domains, Binance-named domains, BlockNovas domain, lure infrastructure
Domain administrator passwords concept
Passwords for highly privileged accounts that can manage users and computers across a Windows domain.
domain names concept
Domain names are human-readable internet addresses used to reach websites and online services.
Domain-Joined concept
A domain-joined device is a computer enrolled in an organization's central Windows identity and management domain.
DownRadar product
An outage-monitoring service that collects reports and information about whether online services are unavailable.
Drop-in product
A special WordPress file that replaces or extends part of WordPress and can load very early in the website startup process.
Drupal product
An open-source content management system used to build and manage websites.
also: Drupal Content Management System
e-commerce concept
E-commerce means buying and selling goods or services online.
Earth Estries threat-actor
A threat-actor group referenced in security reporting.
EIP-7702 protocol
EIP-7702 is an Ethereum proposal that lets a regular account temporarily delegate actions to smart-contract code.
Elliptic organization
Elliptic is a company that analyzes cryptocurrency transactions to help detect fraud, sanctions evasion, and money laundering.
also: Elliptic’s analysis
email account concept
An email account is a user's mailbox and login identity for sending and receiving email.
also: staff email, White House staff member's personal email account
email address concept
An email address is the unique address used to send messages to someone's email account.
email addresses concept
Email addresses are the unique names people use to send and receive email, such as user@example.com.
email authentication checks technique
Email authentication checks are tests such as SPF, DKIM, and DMARC that help verify whether an email really came from the domain it claims.
Embed codes technique
Small pieces of code added to a website so it can load content or services from another provider.
Emergency Response product
Emergency Response is a cybersecurity service that helps an organization investigate and contain a serious active incident.
eMudhra organization
An Indian digital-trust company that issues certificates used to verify identities and secure online connections.
encrypted concept
Encrypted data has been scrambled so that only someone with the right key can read it.
Encrypted connections protocol
Network connections that scramble data so outsiders cannot easily read it while it is being sent.
encryption concept
Encryption is a way of scrambling information so only someone with the right key can read it.
also: encrypted messaging
end of life concept
The point when a vendor stops supporting a product, including no longer providing security fixes.
endpoint concept
An endpoint is a user device such as a laptop, phone, or server that connects to a network.
Endpoint policies concept
Security rules and configuration settings applied to endpoint devices such as laptops, desktops, and servers.
also: endpoint settings
endpoint security concept
Endpoint security is protection for user devices such as laptops, desktops, and phones.
Endpoint sensor coverage concept
The extent to which endpoint security software is installed and collecting activity data on devices.
endpoints concept
Endpoints are user-facing devices such as laptops, desktops, or phones that connect to systems and data.
engagement concept
Engagement means how often people interact with a website, app, message, or notification.
enrichment technique
Enrichment adds extra context to raw security data, such as looking up an IP address, domain, or account to make it more useful.
entry points concept
Entry points are the places where attackers can first get into a system or network.
Enumeration technique
Enumeration is the process of systematically listing users, files, services, or other details about a system.
environment variable concept
An environment variable is a setting stored by an operating system or application that programs can read while they run.
environment variables concept
Environment variables are named settings stored by an operating system or runtime that programs can read while they run.
also: names of environment variables associated with sensitive credentials, standard environment variables, Environment-variable values
eth concept
The standard network interface naming prefix for Ethernet devices in Linux and Unix-like systems.
ethereum
Ethereum is a blockchain platform used for cryptocurrency, smart contracts, and decentralized applications.
evade detection technique
To evade detection means to hide malicious activity so security tools or analysts do not notice it.
event concept
An event is something that happens in a system, such as a login, file change, alert, or configuration update.
also: events, 400-field event
event logs concept
Event logs are records created by computers and applications that show important actions, errors, and security activity.
Event Names concept
Event names are labels that identify the kind of action recorded in a system log.
Exceptions concept
Exceptions are errors or unusual conditions that software handles while running.
Exchange product
Exchange usually refers to Microsoft Exchange, Microsoft's email and calendar server platform.
Exchange Online product
Exchange Online is Microsoft’s cloud-hosted email and calendar service in Microsoft 365.
Execute arbitrary code technique
To execute arbitrary code means an attacker can make a system run commands or software of their choosing.
Execute code concept
Execute code means to make a computer run instructions, which is dangerous if an attacker can run their own code.
Execution technique
Execution is the stage where an attacker runs code or commands on a target system.
Execution records concept
Logs or records that show whether an automated task or action was attempted, completed, failed, or is still pending.
Executive Office for U.S. Trustees organization
The Executive Office for U.S. Trustees is a U.S. Justice Department office that administers the U.S. Trustee Program.
also: DOJ’s bankruptcy office
exfiltration technique
Exfiltration is the unauthorized removal or theft of data from a system or organization.
exploit technique
An exploit is code or a method that takes advantage of a security flaw to make something happen that should not be allowed.
exploit chain technique
A sequence of multiple security exploits used one after another to break into a system step by step.
exploit code tool
Exploit code is software written to take advantage of a security flaw in a system or application.
exploitation technique
Exploitation is taking advantage of a weakness in software or people to gain unauthorized access or control.
exploitation attempts technique
Exploitation attempts are tries to take advantage of a software weakness to gain access, run code, or cause harm.
Exploitation in the wild concept
Exploitation in the wild means attackers are actively using a vulnerability against real targets, not just testing it in a lab.
Exploited technique
Exploited means attackers successfully took advantage of a weakness in software or a system.
exploited in the wild concept
Exploited in the wild means attackers are actively using a vulnerability against real targets, not just in a lab.
Exposed concept
Accessible in a way that could allow a threat to reach or affect a system.
exposed credentials concept
Login details that have been accidentally published or stolen, granting unauthorized access.
Exposed Data concept
Information that may have been viewed, copied, or made accessible to people who were not supposed to have it.
Exposure management platform product
An exposure management platform helps organizations find, prioritize, and reduce security weaknesses across their systems.
Exposure prioritization technique
The process of deciding which security risks should be addressed first based on their likely impact and urgency.
Exposure window concept
An exposure window is the period of time when a system or data is vulnerable to attack or unauthorized access.
extension ID concept
An extension ID is a unique identifier assigned to a browser extension.
extension update concept
An extension update is a new version of a browser add-on, which can fix bugs or introduce new behavior.
extension.js tool
extension.js is a JavaScript file name commonly used for browser or editor extension code and may be referenced as a suspicious artifact.
External hard drives product
Portable storage devices that connect to a computer and hold digital files.
External models concept
External models are AI models hosted or controlled outside an organization’s own systems.
fake companies concept
Organizations falsely presented as real businesses to deceive people.
Fake Job Assessment Portals technique
Fake job assessment portals are fraudulent websites that pretend to test job candidates in order to trick them into sharing information or running harmful software.
also: assessment portal
fake job interviews technique
Fake job interviews are fraudulent recruiting conversations used to trick victims into sharing information or installing malicious software.
also: fake job interview
fake job offers technique
Fake job offers are fraudulent recruiting messages used to trick people into sharing information, installing malware, or sending money.
Fake Stock-Trading Project technique
A fake stock-trading project is a fraudulent software or coding project presented as an investment-related opportunity to trick someone into running malicious code.
fake websites concept
Fake websites are lookalike or fraudulent sites made to trick visitors into giving up money, passwords, or information.
fallback concept
A fallback is a backup option used when the preferred option is unavailable or fails.
false negative concept
A missed alert where a genuine malicious activity goes undetected by security tools, posing a serious risk.
false positive concept
An alert that mistakenly flags benign activity as malicious, causing unnecessary work and potentially distracting from real threats.
false positives concept
False positives are alerts that incorrectly label harmless activity as suspicious or malicious.
fbi organization
The FBI is the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation, which investigates cybercrime and national security threats.
FBI affidavit concept
An FBI affidavit is a sworn written statement used by the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation in legal proceedings.
also: 2014 FBI affidavit, The FBI affidavit
federal agencies organization
Federal agencies are government organizations that operate at the national level.
Federal Bureau of Investigation organization
The Federal Bureau of Investigation is the main U.S. federal law-enforcement agency that investigates crimes including cybercrime.
also: FBI's Cyber's Most Wanted list
federal civilian agencies organization
Government organizations that provide public services rather than military functions.
Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies organization
Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies are U.S. federal agencies outside the military and intelligence communities that run civilian government functions.
also: FCEB
Federal law enforcement organization
Federal law enforcement refers to national-level police or investigative agencies.
file path concept
The location of a file or folder in a computer's storage system.
also: file paths
filter concept
A filter is a rule that narrows down information so only matching items are shown or acted on.
also: filters, filtering
Financial Accounts concept
Financial accounts are accounts that hold or track money, credit, investments, or other financial assets.
Financial aid disbursements concept
Payments of student financial assistance such as grants or loans.
financial loss concept
Financial loss means losing money because of fraud, theft, business disruption, or other damage.
firewall product
A firewall is a security system that controls what network traffic is allowed in or out.
firewalls product
Firewalls are security systems that control which network traffic is allowed in or out.
flaw concept
A flaw is a weakness or mistake in software, design, or configuration that can cause problems or security risk.
FLAWED other
FLAWED is the name of a report about evaluating AI-generated security patches.
Florida Department of Education organization
The Florida state government agency responsible for public education and related programs.
Florida Department of Law Enforcement organization
A Florida state law-enforcement agency that supports criminal investigations and public-safety operations.
Florida Department of Motor Vehicles organization
A Florida state government agency that manages driver licenses, vehicle registration, and related records.
Florida Department of Motor Vehicles organization
A Florida state government agency that manages driver licenses, vehicle registration, and related records.
Florida Digital Service organization
